title.en: Give to Caesar, Give to God

section: The Parable of the Tenants / Paying the Imperial Tax to Caesar

heading.en: A vineyard story, and a clever trap that failed

body.en: Jesus told a parable: a man planted a vineyard and rented it to tenants, then sent servants to collect his share of the fruit — but the tenants beat, even killed, servant after servant! Finally the owner sent his own beloved son, thinking they would respect him — but they killed him too, throwing him out of the vineyard! Jesus asked: what will the owner do? He will destroy the tenants and give the vineyard to others. The religious leaders understood Jesus was talking about THEM, and wanted to arrest Him, but feared the crowd. Later, Pharisees and Herodians tried to trap Jesus with a clever question: 'Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?' If He said yes, He'd anger the crowds; if no, He'd be accused of rebellion against Rome! Jesus asked for a coin, asking whose image was on it. 'Caesar's,' they said. Jesus replied: 'Give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's.' They were amazed at His answer — the trap had completely failed.

label.en: Activity sheet: Give to Caesar, Give to God

body.en:
Big idea: Jesus exposes religious leadership's rejection of God's messengers (and ultimately His own Son) through a pointed parable, then demonstrates remarkable wisdom under a deliberately constructed political trap — acknowledging legitimate civic obligation while reserving ultimate allegiance for God alone.

Conversation starters: (1) Who do the "servants" and the "son" represent in the vineyard parable? (2) Why was the Caesar/God question such a clever trap — what made it hard to answer either way? (3) What does it look like practically to "give to Caesar" and "give to God" appropriately in your own life?

Pray for wisdom like Jesus showed, navigating difficult questions with both honesty and discernment.
